scenes.line1: How do you run tasks efficiently?
scenes.say: How do you run lots of tasks efficiently without wasting resources? What keeps your code scalable?

scenes.label: Threads
scenes.sub: Thread pools reuse threads to run tasks fast.
scenes.say: Thread pools manage a set of reusable threads. They run tasks without creating new threads each time, saving overhead.
Executors handle thread management and task submission. Work queues store tasks and feed them to worker threads.

scenes.code:
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as pool:
    pool.submit(my_task)
scenes.say: In Python, ThreadPoolExecutor lets you run tasks with a fixed number of threads, avoiding the overhead of creating new ones.

scenes.question: Why not create a new thread for each task?
scenes.right: Creating threads for each task adds overhead and wastes resources. Thread pools avoid this and boost efficiency.
scenes.say: Why not just create a new thread for every task? It adds overhead and wastes resources. Thread pools avoid this and keep things efficient.
